citations.excerpt: There are FOUR (4) questions. Attempt all of them. You have 90 minutes to complete the test. There are 100 marks available.
This is a CLOSED BOOK test. There are FOUR (4) questions. Answer all of them. You have 75 minutes to complete the test. There are 40 marks available.
All your answers must conform to practices emphasised in the lectures and practicals.

recall.a: Planning graphs + timing (Q1), user stories + full use case incl. extensions (Q2), FR/NFR + validity + quantified NFRs (Q3), burn-up + Kanban + Scrum events (Q4). Closed book: memorise shapes, formulae, header fields, validity properties.
recall.q: Map the four 2022 questions to topics and state the closed-book implication.

sections.heading: The shape of the midterm
paras: The 2022 paper (90 minutes, 100 marks, closed book, four questions of 25) is the best predictor available: Q1 planning (waterfall + full network analysis + management use), Q2 functional requirements (stories + a complete use case with flow, extension and task goals), Q3 FR/NFR (distinctions, demolitions, usability rewrite, quantified performance/reliability/other NFRs), Q4 agile (burn-up arithmetic, Kanban reasoning, Scrum backlogs and events). Earlier papers add AOA graphs (2018), restaurant ordering cases (2019), plus testing and version-control questions from topics outside the current lecture set.

sections.heading: Where to start reading
bullets: First: Critical path and slack (highest mark density), Use-case flow (most writing marks), NFR validity (most conceptual marks).
Second: Burn-up charts, Scrum events and backlogs, User stories, Activity graphs.
Third: Ethics theories + professionalism (reasoning marks), SRS/IEEE 830 (background that sharpens every requirement answer).
Drills: 2018 AON/AOA + add-friend case; 2019 restaurant case + NFR set; 2022 full paper under timed conditions.

sections.heading: Coverage honesty

callout.text: Coverage map (evidence-linked): lectures 1-4 + ethics fully supported by slides, worksheets and past papers. 2018 testing questions (equivalence partitioning, JUnit) and the 2019 Git question belong to topics whose lectures are not in this collection — they are indexed as supplementary past-paper evidence, not examined core. External references (Scrum Guide, IEEE 830, ACS Code) support — they never override lecture terminology.

paras: Use the Coverage view to check every concept's evidence: lecture pages, worksheet questions, past-paper appearances and practice items. Unattempted questions and low-rated concepts feed the Review queue automatically.

summary: Four questions, four territories — planning, use cases, NFRs, agile — with ethics reasoning throughout; start with the densest marks and drill all three papers.
title: Midterm study guide and coverage

activities.explanation: Marks density first (graphs, use cases), judgement last (ethics reasoning), then one closed-book rehearsal under time.

distractor.0: The cover says plainly: calculators are not allowed. Arithmetic must be hand-checkable — show working.

activities.explanation: False — closed book, no calculators, 90 minutes, 100 marks. Method marks reward shown working even with slips.

visuals.title: Five-day plan mapped to the four questions
visuals.what: One territory per day, then a timed full paper — the highest-yield order.
visuals.caption: Days mirror the 2022 paper's question order; day 5 integrates under exam conditions.

steps.title: Day 1 · Calculation track
steps.text: WBS → AON → forward/backward passes → slack → Gantt. Drill 2022 Q1 and 2019 Q1 timed.

steps.title: Day 2 · Requirements track
steps.text: Stories → headers → flows → extensions → diagrams. Rewrite the 2018 add-friend and 2022 plot-data cases from memory.

steps.title: Day 3 · NFR validity
steps.text: Five-property checklist on Worksheet 4 items (a)–(j); rewrite two invalid NFRs; quantify one of each family.

steps.title: Day 4 · Agile + ethics
steps.text: Burn-up arithmetic, Kanban reasoning, Scrum events, one harm story with framework + code cited.

steps.title: Day 5 · Full paper, timed
steps.text: 2022 Midterm B in 90 minutes, closed book. Mark against rubrics; missed items join the review queue.
